subject: Evaluating low-touch access options for private deploy: peering / PrivateLink / S2S
messages:
From: netops@fintrust.com
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: alice@cloudhub.io
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask: connecting FinTrust private cluster to Redwood Private tenant

Logan,

Thanks for the quick intro. We’re standing up a private deployment to host inference for a subset of FinTrust services (sensitive PII flows, compliance-bound). Our security team prefers an approach that minimizes our attack surface and makes auditing simple. Ops has asked me to gather pros/cons between three connection modes: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints), and a site-to-site VPN (IPsec/BGP).

Primary constraints:
- No IP overlap with our existing VPCs (we can re-IP but prefer minimal change)
- Strong observability: flow logs + per-client identity in logs if possible
- High-availability with failover time < 5m for production traffic
- Predictable cost (we need to model egress/month)

Can you provide an operational recommendation and a short design matrix (latency, throughput, manageability, security, troubleshooting surface)? We’d also like a sketch of any required changes on our side (NAT, route tables, BGP config).

If easier, happy to do a short workshop — our NetOps and security leads can join.

— Sam (FinTrust NetOps)
From: logan_wright@redwood.ai
To: netops@fintrust.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, alice@cloudhub.io
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: connecting FinTrust private cluster to Redwood Private tenant

Sam — thanks for the clear constraints. I did a quick pass with Kim and Marcus and attached a high-level comparison and an architecture sketch. TL;DR summary up top, followed by operational notes and an optional hybrid suggestion.

TL;DR recommendation (short):
- If you need per-request identity + smallest blast radius: Interface PrivateLink endpoints for control-plane / API traffic.
- For sustained low-latency inference calls from many internal services: VPC Peering when IP overlap is impossible and peering is allowed across accounts/regions; otherwise dedicated S2S (IPsec) with BGP and high-throughput tunnels.
- Practical hybrid: PrivateLink for auth/control + ephemeral site-to-site (WireGuard or IPsec with BGP) for bulk inference and batch jobs. This reduces attack surface while avoiding large cross-account CIDR surgery.

Operational comparison (short matrix):
- Latency: Peering < PrivateLink (small extra hop) < S2S (depends on tunnel endpoints and MTU). Expect peering ~sub-ms within AZ, PrivateLink +1-3ms, managed IPsec +5-20ms depending on path.
- Throughput: Peering removes NAT / ENI limits so highest throughput. PrivateLink throughput per ENI is capped and scales by adding endpoints (operational overhead). S2S can achieve high throughput but requires sizing & HA tunnels.
- Manageability: Peering is simple once ip space is clean. PrivateLink requires endpoint management and security groups. S2S needs key rotation, monitoring, and BGP sessions to be run.
- Troubleshooting surface: Peering = route table checks + flow logs. PrivateLink = endpoint health + SGs + ENI metrics. S2S = IPsec/BGP states + tunnel metrics, potential for MTU fragmentation.

Notes on compliance & observability:
- PrivateLink makes it easy to attach an ENI per endpoint; you can run VPC Flow Logs and add host-based telemetry to tag requests. However, per-client identity requires the application layer (mTLS or delegation headers).
- For auditing, recommend centralizing logs to your SIEM using a dedicated forwarder over the same secure path to preserve L7 identity.

Attached: arch diagram (service plane, control plane), sizing matrix with cost roughs.

If you like, we can do a 30-minute workshop this week (Kim would cover AWS-specific caveats; Marcus will cover the runtime and KV cache implications).

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@fintrust.com, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, alice@cloudhub.io
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: connecting FinTrust private cluster to Redwood Private tenant

Sam / team — adding a few concrete operational constraints from the AWS side and what you’ll need to change on your NetOps runway if you pick each option.

VPC Peering (when feasible):
- Pros: Lowest hop count, minimal per-flow overhead, native route tables, no ENI endpoint scaling. Good for low-latency RPCs.
- Cons: No transitive routing (won’t route via a third VPC), requires non-overlapping CIDRs. Cross-region peering exists but can add charges. You’ll need to add explicit routes in route tables and ensure security groups allow cross-account traffic.
- NetOps tasks for FinTrust: allocate a clean /22 (or larger depending on scope), update route propagation, add monitoring (VPC Flow Logs) to capture traffic.

PrivateLink (interface endpoints):
- Pros: Strong isolation (service owner controls the endpoint) and great security posture for control-plane calls (you get a private DNS name and ENI per AZ), works across accounts without route changes. Easier to limit a narrow surface area.
- Cons: Interface endpoints have per-ENI bandwidth limits and require managing security groups. Additional per-ENI costs and potential per-hour charges. Connections from many clients may need many endpoints or NATing behind a small fleet; that increases operational load.
- NetOps tasks: approve cross-account endpoint service, plan ENI quotas, tighten SG rules, prepare for endpoint scaling.

Site-to-site VPN (IPsec/BGP):
- Pros: Works with existing IP schemas (can NAT if needed), familiar to NetOps teams, can be configured for active/active with BGP and short failover times. Good for bulk transfers and when IP renumbering is infeasible.
- Cons: Additional management (key rotation, patching VPN appliances), can introduce jitter/MTU fragmentation, and debugging tunnels is more complex. Egress charges can be higher depending on topology.
- NetOps tasks: provision tunnels from your edge to our peering endpoints, enable BGP with clear ASNs and prefixes, test fragmentation and MSS, and create runbook for failover.

Hybrid approach (operational recommendation):
- Control-plane (auth, job control, admin APIs): PrivateLink. Keeps smallest possible exposed surface and lets security gate service-level access.
- Data-plane (inference payloads): VPC Peering if you can allocate clean CIDRs and want lowest latency. Otherwise S2S with BGP and active/active tunnels.
- Observability: mirror ENI flow logs + host-level tracing to your SIEM. Use mutual TLS and propagate client identity headers for L7 attribution.

Quick checklist for implementation kickoff:
1) Confirm whether FinTrust can allocate non-overlapping CIDR ranges (preferred).
2) Decide which traffic needs per-request identity vs which can be network-level.
3) Approve ENI quotas and endpoint limits in the account (for PrivateLink).
4) Agree on SLA: what’s acceptable failover time, throughput baseline, and maintenance windows.
5) Schedule a 60-minute runbook tabletop with NetOps + our infra team.

Kimberly Park
Senior Cloud Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: netops@fintrust.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, alice@cloudhub.io
Date: Thu, 16 Dec 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: connecting FinTrust private cluster to Redwood Private tenant

Appreciate the clear breakdown and the hybrid recommendation — that aligns with our threat model. A couple of follow-ups before we lock a workshop:
1) Can you call out any specific BGP timers or IPsec cipher suites you’ve seen work best for low-latency inference (we run a constrained edge and want minimal reconvergence time)?
2) If we do PrivateLink for control-plane only, will the control plane scale automatically with endpoint count, or do we need to request more ENIs ahead of time?
3) Cost ask: can you provide a 12-month rough cost delta for peering vs PrivateLink + S2S hybrid (ballpark numbers are fine, we’ll refine in procurement).

If you can send answers + updated diagram (with the split-plane overlay), we’ll schedule the runbook kickoff next week.

— Sam (FinTrust NetOps)
